title: The big lookout
hookLine: look back down the hill: from salaam on day one to a whole juz' carried in the heart

lines: A WOODEN RAIL, A WORN BENCH.
cards: Some trails end at a lookout: a wooden rail, a worn bench, a little sign naming the peaks. People who've been staring at their boots for hours stand there and go quiet.
Below, you can see the town where you started, small enough to cover with your thumb. Ahead, a further range you didn't know was there. Stand here a minute.
This is the last day of camp five, and the last day of year one.

teach.b: Look back down the hill. Yesterday you gathered the year camp by camp. Up here, you don't need the list; only a few landmarks stand out.
Way down at the bottom, one word: salaam, a greeting that is also a wish. Further up, a seven-verse prayer you learned a piece at a time, long before you heard it called the mother of the book.

teach.h: A WHOLE JUZ', BEGUN IN THE HEART
teach.b: And near the top, a whole juz', thirty-seven surahs, walked backward from An-Nas to An-Naba', carried in the heart, or at least begun there. Notice something else from up here. The path never went straight.
It switched back from words to stories, from stories to practice, from practice to the text, then further in. From below, each turn felt like a new subject.
From here it looks like one road, circling the same few things: God named and remembered, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ walked beside, a book heard aloud. Now look ahead.

teach.h: AHEAD: THE BOOK, SURAH BY SURAH
teach.b: Year two is the book, surah by surah: starting from the Opening and al-Baqarah and reading onward, a little each day, all the way to the edge of the juz' you already know. It's a big range. The method doesn't change.

The Prophet said, as Bukhari records, that the deeds most loved by Allah are the ones done regularly, even if they're small. That's how this hill was climbed: one small day at a time, from salaam to here.

how: Many Muslims keep a small daily portion of Qur'an reading and remembrance rather than occasional long sessions, following the teaching that the deeds most loved by Allah are the regular ones, even if small.

o: a lantern for walking at night
a loaf of bread baked at home
peace, a greeting that is also a wish

games.q: the view from the top — tap the pairs.
p: a juz', walked from An-Nas back

s: year two starts over from salaam
it reads the book surah by surah, from the Opening onward.
the Prophet said the deeds most loved are those done regularly, even if small
children usually learn the Qur'an starting from al-Baqarah
many start at the end, with the short surahs, as this path did.

games.q: you're standing at the top of year one. what does the path ask of you now?
o: rest a moment, then keep reading, a little each day.
games.why: rest, then keep going: the deeds most loved are the regular ones, even if small. year two is the whole book.

practice: Choose the verse that stayed with you most this year, the one you wrote down, a line of al-Fatiha, al-Kawthar, or bismillah itself, and say it once, aloud, slowly, the way you'd speak at the top of a hill.
Then stop, rest, and let the whole year lie behind you like a view. If you pray, you can thank Allah in your own words.

wordCard.voice: Salaam. Peace — the path's very first word, from the same root as Islam and Muslim, seen again from the top of year one. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: peace. the path's first word, from the same root as Islam and Muslim.

carryVoice: Your line: from here you can see. Tomorrow, year two begins. Day three hundred thirty-one, and year one is yours.
